asks: How is the agent's own summary held against the record?
answer: A classifier that a model runs reads the agent's summary beside the facts of its receipt, and gives one opinion on it: matched, mismatch, or nothing in the record shows it. It is an extension, in a computer of its own, and its only tool is the one that gives the opinion. It reads the summary twice: once as written, and once as a list of claims made from the summary by a first call, judged against the receipt by a second call that never reads the summary. The more severe of the two opinions shows beside the summary, marked as that classifier's, and the line of the receipt it rests on is named. Whether that line is in the receipt is checked, and an opinion that rests on no line of it counts as not checked. Whether the summary speaks to a checker is shown on its own: a fixed test on the words, and the first call's opinion. A matched opinion on a summary that speaks to a checker is not shown as matched. The receipt's own lines need no classifier: a failed last test run, code changed after the last test run, files deleted or outside the folder, and a process left running show in every receipt, whatever the summary says. Silo ships no list of fixed phrases that marks a summary matched.
